content.thinking:
This variant reads as a measurement-and-modeling arm, dry and jargon-heavy, emphasizing instruments and reproducibility to boost perceived competence more than warmth or openness—likely raising the trust score by 1.5–2.5, though the jargon risks alienating readers or feeding skepticism toward models themselves.

I'm settling on estimates around: trust_multidimensional +1.7, trust_post +1.2, distrust_post -0.9, modest bumps to funding perceptions and institutional trust (+0.5 and +0.7), belief +0.8, and smaller effects on policy and behavioral measures given the objective, non-advocacy framing. Since this seems to be one of two versions of this arm and reads especially jargon-heavy, I'm leaning toward the lower end of my competence estimate.

content.text: {"reasoning_summary": "This arm is a dry, expository description of climate science's instruments, quantitative methods, and reproducibility. Its direct target is the competence dimension of trust (and secondarily integrity via 'empirical data rather than subjective impressions'), so I expect a modest positive effect on the fresh multidimensional trust battery, driven mainly by the competence and integrity subscales while benevolence/openness move little. Heavy jargon (disdrometers, wavelet analysis, support vector machines) reduces processing fluency and offers no narrative or messenger-credibility advantage, and the emphasis on 'models and simulations' can even feed a small amount of model skepticism among the initially distrustful, so I place it slightly below the average trust arm rather than at the top. Re-asked single items (trust_post, belief_post) are shrunk by pre-treatment anchoring, and the text says nothing about funding, policy, or scientists' societal role, so those outcomes get only small spillovers via generalized trust. parsed_output.reasoning_summary: This arm is a dry, expository description of climate science's instruments, quantitative methods, and reproducibility. Its direct target is the competence dimension of trust (and secondarily integrity via 'empirical data rather than subjective impressions'), so I expect a modest positive effect on the fresh multidimensional trust battery, driven mainly by the competence and integrity subscales while benevolence/openness move little. Heavy jargon (disdrometers, wavelet analysis, support vector machines) reduces processing fluency and offers no narrative or messenger-credibility advantage, and the emphasis on 'models and simulations' can even feed a small amount of model skepticism among the initially distrustful, so I place it slightly below the average trust arm rather than at the top. Re-asked single items (trust_post, belief_post) are shrunk by pre-treatment anchoring, and the text says nothing about funding, policy, or scientists' societal role, so those outcomes get only small spillovers via generalized trust. Distal outcomes (concern, policy, behavior) get sub-point effects, and incentivized behaviors get near-zero effects consistent with megastudy evidence (a few cents; under one percentage point on sign-up).
